title: Dutch AI Conference · speaker call
fundingSummary: Selected international speakers: organizer-booked travel, airport transfers, two hotel nights, conference access, speaker dinner and afterparty. Workshop speakers receive three hotel nights.
costs: Visa, insurance and meals outside the stated package are not explicitly covered. No application fee stated.
eligibility: Open to all ages. Selection is competitive; proposals can cover applied AI, architecture, ethics, team management and soft skills.
summary: Contribute a practical talk and meet engineers and leaders. The AI conference is one day; sister conferences run March 16–19.
caution: Core travel and accommodation are explicit, but not every incidental expense. Confirm exact itinerary with the organizer before booking.

title: DevSum · speaker call
fundingSummary: Selected speakers receive travel and hotel coverage and free conference admission.
costs: Meal, visa, insurance and reimbursement-cap details were not established in the inspected call.
eligibility: Competitive talk selection. No age restriction identified in the inspected call; verify any additional requirements before submission.
summary: Two-day developer conference with a funded speaking route.
caution: CFP closes December 8 at 23:59 CET. Detailed coverage and payment arrangements need confirmation.

title: Pixel Pioneers · speaker call
fundingSummary: Speaking fee plus travel and hotel support are stated by the organizer.
costs: Airfare limits, incidental expenses and exact payment arrangements were not verified.
eligibility: Competitive speaker selection; front-end and UX perspectives. No age restriction identified in the inspected call.
summary: Compact conference bringing together web developers and designers.
caution: Travel support is not an independently confirmed promise to pay every trip expense.

title: AILA International Fellowship
host: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)
fundingSummary: Extremely limited full or partial tuition scholarships. Published application guidance generally prioritizes nonprofit and developing-country applicants.
costs: Standard tuition: US$5,000. Travel and lodging are not covered; budget for these even if tuition is waived.
eligibility: International and corporate professionals can apply. Scholarship eligibility and selection are separate from programme eligibility.
summary: Five-day executive leadership programme exploring global strategy and policy.
caution: Not a fully funded trip. The inspected 2026 application explicitly excludes travel/lodging assistance; check the 2027 award terms before accepting.

title: Future Diplomats Forum · advertised scholarships
fundingSummary: Private organizer advertises 50 full scholarships including round-trip airfare, twin-share hotel, meals, transfers and forum access; its FAQ also lists visa costs.
costs: US$16.50 application fee, non-refundable and non-transferable for funded categories. Travel must be paid upfront; policy says reimbursement takes 4–8 weeks after attendance and bank-detail submission.
eligibility: Published age range: 18–45. Competitive application considered across three funding tiers. Results advertised for November 25.
summary: Short diplomacy forum with advertised funding; a lead for further due diligence rather than an institutional endorsement.
caution: No official UN/UN Geneva/UNESCO partnership or vetting established. No airfare cap found in inspected terms, which does not guarantee unlimited reimbursement. Confirm written award and refund terms before spending.

title: Youth Global Forum · advertised scholarships
host: Centre for Global Dialogue and Leadership (CGDL)
fundingSummary: Private organizer advertises 30 funded places including hotel, meals and airfare support.
costs: US$16.99 non-refundable application fee. Airfare reimbursement is capped at an amount set by CGDL; the inspected terms do not publish the cap. Travel is normally not advanced.
eligibility: Published age range: 16–46. Competitive funded-place selection.
summary: Four-day international forum with a partially funded or capped-reimbursement route.
caution: No official UN/UNESCO partnership or vetting established. Institutional visits depend on availability and approval. Do not treat the advertised “fully funded” label as guaranteed full airfare.

title: World Bank Youth Summit · next pitch cycle
fundingSummary: The 2026 competition said travel, lodging and a nominal stipend may be provided for one representative per finalist team, subject to eligibility and availability.
costs: Other team members and general attendance are not automatically funded. Visa remains the participant’s responsibility; support letters may be offered.
eligibility: Past cycle: ages 18–35 and World Bank member-country nationality. Idea-stage entries and working professionals were eligible. New-cycle terms must be rechecked.
summary: Institutional pitch competition worth watching for a concrete development or technology solution.
caution: No verified 2027 application call found. Last verified summit was June 11–12, 2026 and has passed. No separate “Tech Leader Track” was established.

title: One Young World · Tokyo scholarship watch
fundingSummary: Past corporate scholarships have covered airfare, accommodation, summit access and specified meals. Each award has its own terms.
costs: 2027 scholarship terms and application fees, if any, have not been established. Some programmes include extra pre-summit days.
eligibility: Many awards target ages 18–30 but some past schemes considered over-30 applicants. Relevant demonstrated impact, nationality and residence rules vary by sponsor.
summary: Four-day global summit with multiple competitive scholarship programmes.
caution: Summit dates are announced, but matching 2027 scholarship calls were not verified open. Past awards are not current offers or proof of age eligibility.

title: Salzburg Global · programme watch
fundingSummary: Programme-specific scholarships can cover session costs and room/board. Travel support exists only in some cases.
costs: Travel or other expenses may remain self-funded. Institutional support is encouraged where available.
eligibility: Selection depends on the programme’s subject matter and professional contribution. No blanket short-course scholarship for corporate participants.
summary: Small residential discussions bringing different professions together.
caution: No verified open call meeting a five-day maximum and broadly applicable eligibility in this scan. Cultural Futures Forum 2027 was closed; other inspected calls were six days or restricted by residence/theme.

title: IMF Youth Fellowship · next-call watch
fundingSummary: Historical editions included funded attendance, but current award terms have not been established.
costs: Unknown until a new official call is published.
eligibility: Historical age and leadership requirements must not be assumed to apply to a future edition.
summary: Potential IMF route when a new official recruitment cycle is published.
caution: No verified open 2026/2027 call found. An alumni reunion is not a new fellowship application.

title: IMF CEF courses · eligibility restriction
host: IMF Middle East Center for Economics and Finance
fundingSummary: Eligible nominated government officials may receive economy travel, hotel, meals and an incidental allowance.
costs: Allowances may not cover all additional expenses.
eligibility: Standard residential training explicitly excludes commercial-bank employees and requires eligible government-agency employment and official nomination.
summary: Retained as an eligibility note to avoid repeatedly recommending the wrong route.
caution: Commercial-bank seniority or regional residence does not satisfy government-official eligibility.

title: RIPE Fellowship · RIPE 94 Vilnius / RIPE 95 Madrid
location: Vilnius, Lithuania (or Madrid, Spain in Nov 2027)
fundingSummary: Free meeting ticket, travel and accommodation, plus coaching, public-speaking training and a peer group.
costs: No stipend mentioned. Visa and some travel costs may not be fully covered; reimbursement is not possible for residents of certain countries.
eligibility: 18+ and resident in the RIPE NCC service region (the UAE is in it). You must work or study in a field directly tied to Internet technical coordination/operations. General IT or software roles alone are not enough. You must pass the free RIPE 101 course quiz before you are invited to apply.
summary: A week at Europe’s main network-operator meeting: routing, DNS, security, policy. A strong fit only if your bank role touches infrastructure, networking or Internet security.
caution: Deadline is 23 Nov 2026 and the RIPE 101 quiz comes first, so start now. Frame your infrastructure/ops responsibilities clearly.

title: dxday 2027 AI Edition · speaker call
fundingSummary: Free ticket, speakers’ dinner, single hotel room for up to 3 nights (if travelling from outside Europe) and travel refunded up to €500 from outside Europe.
costs: Flights from Dubai may exceed the €500 cap. Visa and meals outside the dinner are on you.
eligibility: No age limit. Talks should come from people who have “done the work”; first-time speakers are welcome and get coaching. Sessions are 35–40 minutes in English.
summary: One-day applied-AI conference. A talk on running AI delivery inside a large regulated bank would fit well.
caution: Check the travel cap against real fares before accepting.

title: KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2027 · free pass scholarship
fundingSummary: Complimentary All-Access pass, including CNCF-hosted co-located events.
costs: Travel, hotel and visa are your responsibility.
eligibility: For people who could not attend without registration help. Past cycles had diversity, need-based and maintainer tracks. No age limit stated.
summary: The largest cloud-native and platform-engineering conference in Europe, with a growing AI-infrastructure track.
caution: The 2027 form is a SurveyMonkey link; confirm it on the Linux Foundation event page. Passes can run out before the deadline, so apply early.

title: ICANN Fellowship · next newcomer round
location: Rotating worldwide (next newcomer-eligible meeting: ICANN90, late 2027)
fundingSummary: Fellows receive travel assistance to attend an ICANN public meeting, plus mentoring and onboarding into the policy community.
costs: ICANN’s page does not itemise airfare, hotel and stipend. Check the terms when the round opens.
eligibility: 21+, all regions and sectors. You must complete the ICANN Learn course(s). The ICANN89 round (5 Nov–5 Dec 2026) is for alumni only, so a first-time applicant should aim for the following round.
summary: A route into global Internet policy (domain names, DNS security, AI and identity debates) with a strong alumni network.
caution: Past annual-meeting rounds opened around March, but no date is announced yet. Do the ICANN Learn courses now.

title: GLOBSEC Young Leaders Forum 2027
fundingSummary: Funding for 2027 is not yet published. Check the call for travel and accommodation support.
costs: Unknown until the 2027 call opens.
eligibility: Past editions: ages 25–35 (you qualify at 31), with a CV and motivation letter. The 2026 deadline was 6 March 2026.
summary: A young-leaders track alongside GLOBSEC Forum, one of Central Europe’s main security and geopolitics conferences, with policy, tech and business participants.
caution: Age range and funding come from aggregator listings of past calls. Verify on globsec.org when the 2027 call appears, likely early 2027.

title: WEF Forum of Young Global Leaders · nomination watch
location: Global, with sessions in Geneva and elsewhere
fundingSummary: Not published per participant. Verify with the Forum if nominated.
costs: Unknown.
eligibility: Under 40. Referral and nomination only: unsolicited applications are not accepted. A third-party listing gave a Class of 2027 birth window of 1988–1998, with nominations closing 10 May 2026.
summary: WEF’s flagship network for leaders under 40. Worth knowing about for the long term: senior leaders, alumni or WEF partners (Emirates NBD may be one) can nominate you.
caution: Realistic only with a strong external profile and a nominator. Treat it as a long-term goal.

title: Munich Young Leaders · Munich Security Conference
fundingSummary: Not stated on the programme page.
costs: Unknown.
eligibility: Under 40, excellent English, foreign- and security-policy experience, and engagement beyond your job. German embassies each propose up to three candidates; you cannot apply directly.
summary: A small cohort that joins the Munich Security Conference each February.
caution: Low fit unless your work moves toward tech/AI security policy. Listed so you know the route exists.

title: International Visitor Leadership Program (IVLP)
fundingSummary: A U.S. government exchange. The State Department organises and funds the programme.
costs: Confirm per diem and incidentals with the embassy if nominated.
eligibility: No application: U.S. embassies nominate mid-career professionals and emerging leaders. Projects often cover tech, innovation, entrepreneurship and finance.
summary: Up to three weeks of meetings with U.S. counterparts. Build a relationship with the U.S. Embassy in Abu Dhabi (or Yerevan) to be considered.
caution: Usually up to 3 weeks, a bit longer than your 2-week preference.

title: World Governments Summit 2027
fundingSummary: Local to you, so no travel. Registration terms for 2027 are not yet published.
costs: Attendance has historically been invitation-led. Check whether Emirates NBD has delegate places.
eligibility: Invitation or registration once announced.
summary: Heads of government, ministers and tech CEOs in Dubai, with heavy AI-in-government programming.
caution: Watch worldgovernmentssummit.org for registration. Ask your bank’s government-relations team.

title: GITEX Global 2026 + Expand North Star
fundingSummary: Local. Third-party listings say the Expand North Star (startup) pass is free and the GITEX visitor pass is about AED 630.
costs: Prices are unverified on gitex.com. Vendors and partners often hand out free visitor codes, and Emirates NBD may have some.
eligibility: Open registration.
summary: The region’s biggest tech and AI show, held for the first time at Expo City in December.
caution: Dates and venue come from aggregators that disagree slightly; confirm on gitex.com.

title: AI for Good Global Summit 2027
fundingSummary: Pass prices for 2027 are not yet published. A free tier was reported by a third party.
costs: Travel and Geneva hotels are expensive and not covered. Much of the programme is streamed free online.
eligibility: Open registration. Speaker, startup and partner calls run separately.
summary: The UN’s main AI summit, which fits your AI-leadership focus. The Swiss-hosted Geneva AI Summit takes place the same week.
caution: An ITU letter gives 21–24 June and other materials say the week of 21–25 June. Confirm on aiforgood.itu.int.

title: PyCon US 2027 · travel grant watch
fundingSummary: Grants usually cover airfare and similar travel costs, but the budget only covers part of the applicants.
costs: Amounts vary, and not every applicant receives full travel.
eligibility: Open to anyone; no age limit. Past cycles opened around December and closed in February.
summary: The main Python conference, with strong AI/ML, data and engineering-leadership talks.
caution: 2027 dates have not been announced. Sign up for the PyCon US newsletter.

title: BlueDot Impact · AGI Strategy (cohort course)
fundingSummary: Free. Each week combines 2–3 hours of reading with a 2-hour live facilitated discussion.
costs: Your time only.
eligibility: Application needed; about half of applicants were admitted in a recent cohort. It is the gateway to BlueDot’s AI Governance course.
summary: A well-regarded free AI-strategy and governance course with a strong professional network. Good for AI-leadership credibility.
caution: Cohorts run on a rolling basis; check the course page for the next deadline.

title: UNESCO Global MOOC on the Ethics of AI
fundingSummary: Free, with a shareable certificate.
costs: Your time only.
eligibility: Open to all.
summary: Ten modules on responsible AI. Useful framing for AI governance in a regulated bank.
caution: Sources disagree on whether it is hosted on UNESCO OpenLearning, Coursera or both. Use the official UNESCO link.

title: AI For Everyone (Andrew Ng)
fundingSummary: Learning materials are usually free (audit or “no certificate” mode). The certificate is paid.
costs: Coursera certificate fee if you want one. Financial aid is possible.
eligibility: Open to all.
summary: A short non-technical course for leading AI initiatives in an organisation. Quick to finish; useful for briefing teams.
caution: You may already know this material. Skip it if it is too basic.

title: Learn German free · Nicos Weg A1–B1
fundingSummary: Completely free, with a level test and a DW certificate at the end of each level.
costs: None.
eligibility: Open to all, and beginner-friendly.
summary: A video-series German course from Germany’s public broadcaster, built with the Federal Employment Agency.
caution: Combine it with conversation practice; Goethe-Institut courses in Dubai are paid.

title: Basic Spanish 1–3 (edX)
fundingSummary: Free audit track. The verified certificate costs roughly $29–40.
costs: Audit access may be time-limited.
eligibility: Open to all; no prior Spanish needed.
summary: A university-made beginner sequence for English speakers, in three parts.
caution: Reviewers say the listening is fast and practice is light. For in-person classes, UCAM Dubai is the Gulf’s Instituto Cervantes-accredited centre (paid).

title: Introduction to Italian (FutureLearn)
fundingSummary: Free limited-time access on FutureLearn. Unlimited access and a certificate are paid.
costs: Upgrade fee is optional.
eligibility: Open to all; aimed at absolute beginners.
summary: A beginner course from Italy’s specialist university for teaching Italian to foreigners.
caution: Free access periods on FutureLearn are limited, so finish within the window.
